system: You are a helpful assistant. Notes and summaries can drift from what they summarise. Before you rely on any specific (a number, a condition, who is responsible, what applies to whom), check it against the source document itself; where the two differ, the source governs.
message:
Earlier you read the document below and made these notes on it:

<notes>
Orchard & Vale's Travel and Expenses Policy (FIN-07, from 1 May 2026) applies to partners, employees and day-rate contractors. Expenses must be wholly, exclusively and necessarily for business and reasonable; client-recharged costs follow the client's policy if it's stricter. Rail is standard class by default, but first class may be booked for business journeys where it is more comfortable for working; book via the travel portal seven days ahead where possible. Flights under six hours are economy; premium economy for longer flights needs Practice Head approval. Mileage is 45p for the first 10,000 business miles and 25p after; commuting doesn't count; parking and congestion charges are covered, fines are not. Hotel rooms are capped at £150 per night including breakfast, excluding VAT; anything above needs prior Practice Head approval, with overseas rates set by Finance. Overnight trips carry a £45 daily meal allowance, and day trips over ten hours up to £15 for an evening meal. Alcohol is only covered for pre-approved client entertainment. Tips of up to 10% are reimbursable, as are automatic service charges. Client entertainment needs prior Partner approval and must be logged. Claims go through the app within 60 days, receipts for £10+, approved by your line manager and paid with the next payroll.
</notes>

Here is the document itself, for reference:

<document>
ORCHARD & VALE CONSULTING LLP — TRAVEL AND EXPENSES POLICY (Policy FIN-07, effective 1 May 2026)

1. Purpose. This policy sets out what business expenses the firm will reimburse and how to claim them. It applies to all partners, employees and contractors engaged on day-rate terms who travel on firm business.

2. General principles. Expenses must be wholly, exclusively and necessarily incurred on firm business, and must be reasonable. Where an expense is rechargeable to a client, the client's own expenses policy applies if it is stricter than this one.

3. Rail travel. Standard class is the default for all rail journeys. First-class travel may be booked only where the scheduled journey time is more than three hours in each direction, or where the first-class fare is cheaper than the standard fare at the time of booking. Tickets should be booked through the firm's travel portal at least seven days in advance where possible.

4. Air travel. Economy class for flights under six hours. Premium economy may be booked for flights of six hours or more, with Practice Head approval.

5. Driving. Use of a private car is reimbursed at 45p per mile for the first 10,000 business miles in the tax year and 25p per mile thereafter. Ordinary commuting between home and your normal office is not business mileage. Parking and congestion charges are reimbursable; parking and speeding fines are not.

6. Hotels. The maximum room rate, including breakfast and excluding VAT, is £150 per night in Greater London and £110 per night elsewhere in the UK. Rates above these caps require written approval from the Practice Head before booking. Overseas rates are set by the Finance team per city.

7. Meals. When travelling overnight, a daily meal allowance of up to £45 applies (receipts required). Day trips of more than ten hours away from your normal workplace allow up to £15 for an evening meal. Alcohol is reimbursable only as part of client entertainment approved in advance.

8. Tips and service charges. Discretionary tips and gratuities are not reimbursable. A service charge that is automatically added to a bill is reimbursable as part of the bill.

9. Client entertainment. All client entertainment must be approved in advance by a Partner and recorded in the gifts and hospitality register, including the names of attendees.

10. Claims. Claims must be submitted through the expenses app within 60 days of the expense being incurred. Itemised receipts are required for all expenses of £10 or more. Claims are approved by your line manager and paid with the next monthly payroll after approval. Claims submitted more than 60 days late will not be paid except in exceptional circumstances agreed by the Finance Director.

11. Corporate cards. Holders of corporate cards must reconcile transactions in the expenses app within 30 days of the statement date. Personal spending on a corporate card is not permitted.

12. Breaches. Deliberately false claims will be treated as gross misconduct.
</document>

A few questions from someone who needs to act on this:
1. I'm going London to Birmingham (about 1 hour 20 minutes) and want to work on the train. Can I book first class at the normal first-class fare?
2. I need a hotel in Manchester costing £135 a night including breakfast (excl. VAT). Can I book without extra approval?
3. I left a 10% tip on a £40 overnight-trip dinner. Can I claim the £4?
4. What mileage rate applies to the first 10,000 business miles?
response:
Checked against the policy itself (FIN-07). My earlier notes were wrong on three of these points, so the corrected answers are below.

**1. First class, London to Birmingham (about 1h20): No.**
Section 3 allows first class only if the scheduled journey is **more than three hours each way**, or the **first-class fare is cheaper than the standard fare** when you book. Neither applies here, so book standard class. Wanting to work on the train is not a criterion; my notes were wrong on this. Book through the travel portal at least seven days ahead where possible.

**2. Manchester hotel at £135/night: No, you need approval first.**
Section 6 sets a cap of **£150 only for Greater London**. Elsewhere in the UK, including Manchester, the cap is **£110 per night**, including breakfast and excluding VAT. At £135 you need **written approval from your Practice Head before booking**. My notes wrongly applied the £150 figure everywhere.

**3. The £4 tip: No.**
Section 8 says **discretionary tips and gratuities are not reimbursable**. Only a service charge added automatically to the bill can be claimed. My notes wrongly said tips up to 10% were covered. You can claim the £40 dinner itself, since it falls within the £45 daily overnight meal allowance. You'll need an itemised receipt because it's over £10.

**4. Mileage rate: 45p per mile** for the first 10,000 business miles in the tax year, then 25p per mile. Commuting between home and your normal office doesn't count. My notes had this right.
